title: Quasi-finiteness at a prime passes along a square with surjective tensor map
statement: Let $R\to S$, $R\to R'$, $R'\to S'$ and $S\to S'$ be homomorphisms of commutative rings with $R\to S\to S'$ equal to $R\to R'\to S'$. Assume that $R\to S$ is of finite type [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra] and that $S'$ is generated as a ring by the images of $S$ and of $R'$ in the sense that every element of $S'$ is a finite sum $\sum_i \sigma_i\rho_i$ with $\sigma_i$ in the image of $S$ and $\rho_i$ in the image of $R'$ (equivalently, the map $S\otimes_RR'\to S'$, $s\otimes r'\mapsto \sigma\rho$, is surjective); then $R'\to S'$ is of finite type. Let $\mathfrak q'\subset S'$ be a prime ideal, and let $\mathfrak q\subset S$, $\mathfrak p'\subset R'$ be its inverse images. If $R\to S$ is quasi-finite at $\mathfrak q$ [def-weil-pbc-ring-map-quasi-finite-at-prime], then $R'\to S'$ is quasi-finite at $\mathfrak q'$.

proof.text: *Setting and finite type.* Write $\varphi:R\to S$, $\psi:R\to R'$, $\rho:R'\to S'$, $\sigma:S\to S'$, so $\sigma\circ\varphi=\rho\circ\psi$. Put $\mathfrak p=\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)\subset R$. Then $\psi^{-1}(\mathfrak p')=\psi^{-1}\rho^{-1}(\mathfrak q')=\varphi^{-1}\sigma^{-1}(\mathfrak q')=\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)=\mathfrak p$: the primes form the commutative diagram of the source. If $s_1,\dots,s_n$ generate $S$ as an $R$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], then $\sigma(s_1),\dots,\sigma(s_n)$ generate $S'$ as an $R'$-algebra: an element of $S'$ is $\sum_i\sigma(t_i)\rho(r'_i)$ with $t_i\in S$, $r'_i\in R'$, each $t_i$ is a polynomial in the $s_j$ with coefficients in $\varphi(R)$, and $\sigma(\varphi(a))=\rho(\psi(a))$; so $R'\to S'$ is of finite type, and quasi-finiteness of $R'\to S'$ at $\mathfrak q'$ is defined [def-weil-pbc-ring-map-quasi-finite-at-prime].

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00PN (lemma-four-rings, line 30293), the statement and its diagram of primes; finite type of $R'\to S'$ is implicit in the source (it is needed for 'quasi-finite at $\mathfrak q'$' to be defined, Definition Tag 00PL)

proof.text: *The fibre rings and the map between them.* Let $\kappa(\mathfrak p)=R_{\mathfrak p}/\mathfrak pR_{\mathfrak p}$ and $\kappa(\mathfrak p')=R'_{\mathfrak p'}/\mathfrak p'R'_{\mathfrak p'}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Since $\psi(R\setminus\mathfrak p)\subseteq R'\setminus\mathfrak p'$ and $\psi(\mathfrak p)\subseteq\mathfrak p'$ (step 1), $a/t\mapsto\psi(a)/\psi(t)$ is a well defined ring map $R_{\mathfrak p}\to R'_{\mathfrak p'}$ sending $\mathfrak pR_{\mathfrak p}$ into $\mathfrak p'R'_{\mathfrak p'}$, hence induces a field homomorphism $\iota:\kappa(\mathfrak p)\to\kappa(\mathfrak p')$ with $\iota(\bar a)=\overline{\psi(a)}$ for $a\in R$. Let $F=S\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ and $F'=S'\otimes_{R'}\kappa(\mathfrak p')$ be the fibre rings, $j:S\to F$, $s\mapsto s\otimes1$, and $j':S'\to F'$, $s'\mapsto s'\otimes1$. The ring maps $j'\circ\sigma:S\to F'$ and $\kappa(\mathfrak p)\xrightarrow{\iota}\kappa(\mathfrak p')\to F'$, $\lambda\mapsto1\otimes\iota(\lambda)$, are $R$-algebra maps: for $a\in R$ the first sends $\varphi(a)$ to $\sigma\varphi(a)\otimes1=\rho\psi(a)\otimes1=1\otimes\overline{\psi(a)}$, the second sends $\bar a$ to $1\otimes\iota(\bar a)=1\otimes\overline{\psi(a)}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property] (2) there is a ring map $\alpha:F\to F'$ with $\alpha(s\otimes\lambda)=\sigma(s)\otimes\iota(\lambda)$; in particular $\alpha\circ j=j'\circ\sigma$ and $\alpha(\lambda x)=\iota(\lambda)\alpha(x)$ for $\lambda\in\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, $x\in F$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00PN (lemma-four-rings, line 30293): the canonical map $(S\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p))\otimes_{\kappa(\mathfrak p)}\kappa(\mathfrak p')\to S'\otimes_{R'}\kappa(\mathfrak p')$; here written as the map $\alpha$ from the first factor, compatible with $\kappa(\mathfrak p)\to\kappa(\mathfrak p')$

proof.text: *$F'$ is spanned over $\kappa(\mathfrak p')$ by $\alpha(F)$.* Every element of $F'=S'\otimes_{R'}\kappa(\mathfrak p')$ is a finite sum of tensors $s'\otimes\mu=\mu\cdot(s'\otimes1)$ with $s'\in S'$, $\mu\in\kappa(\mathfrak p')$. By hypothesis $s'=\sum_i\sigma(t_i)\rho(r'_i)$ with $t_i\in S$, $r'_i\in R'$, and since the tensor product is over $R'$, $\sigma(t_i)\rho(r'_i)\otimes1=\sigma(t_i)\otimes\overline{r'_i}=\overline{r'_i}\cdot\alpha(t_i\otimes1)$, where $\overline{r'_i}$ is the image of $r'_i$ in $\kappa(\mathfrak p')$. Hence every $x\in F'$ is a finite sum $x=\sum_k\mu_k\alpha(f_k)$ with $\mu_k\in\kappa(\mathfrak p')$, $f_k\in F$. (This is the surjectivity of $F\otimes_{\kappa(\mathfrak p)}\kappa(\mathfrak p')\to F'$ in the source.)

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00PN (lemma-four-rings, line 30293): 'Because $S\otimes_RR'\to S'$ is surjective the canonical map $(S\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p))\otimes_{\kappa(\mathfrak p)}\kappa(\mathfrak p')\to S'\otimes_{R'}\kappa(\mathfrak p')$ is surjective'

proof.text: *The points of the two fibres.* By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-ring-primes-bijection] let $\overline{\mathfrak q}\subset F$ be the unique prime with $j^{-1}(\overline{\mathfrak q})=\mathfrak q$ (as $\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)=\mathfrak p$) and $\overline{\mathfrak q}'\subset F'$ the unique prime with $j'^{-1}(\overline{\mathfrak q}')=\mathfrak q'$ (as $\rho^{-1}(\mathfrak q')=\mathfrak p'$); these are the points of [def-weil-pbc-ring-map-quasi-finite-at-prime]. The ideal $\alpha^{-1}(\overline{\mathfrak q}')$ is a prime of $F$, and $j^{-1}(\alpha^{-1}(\overline{\mathfrak q}'))=(\alpha j)^{-1}(\overline{\mathfrak q}')=(j'\sigma)^{-1}(\overline{\mathfrak q}')=\sigma^{-1}(\mathfrak q')=\mathfrak q$ (step 2). By the injectivity of $\mathfrak Q\mapsto j^{-1}(\mathfrak Q)$ in [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-ring-primes-bijection], $\alpha^{-1}(\overline{\mathfrak q}')=\overline{\mathfrak q}$. So for $x\in F$: $x\notin\overline{\mathfrak q}$ implies $\alpha(x)\notin\overline{\mathfrak q}'$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00PN (lemma-four-rings, line 30293): 'The map $S'\otimes_{R'}\kappa(\mathfrak p')\to\kappa(\mathfrak q')$ factors through $S'_1$ ... because the map $S\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)\to\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ factors through $S_1$'; Remark Tag 00E6 (remark-fundamental-diagram) for the points of the fibre

proof.text: *An idempotent cutting out $\overline{\mathfrak q}$.* $F$ is a $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$-algebra of finite type [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], generated by the $j(s_i)$ for generators $s_i$ of $S$ over $R$ (every $s\otimes\lambda=\lambda\,j(s)$). By hypothesis $R\to S$ is quasi-finite at $\mathfrak q$, i.e. $\{\overline{\mathfrak q}\}$ is open in $\operatorname{Spec}F$ [def-weil-pbc-ring-map-quasi-finite-at-prime]. By [lem-weil-pbc-isolated-prime-finite-type-algebra-residue-finite] (with $k=\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, $B=F$) $\overline{\mathfrak q}$ is a maximal ideal of $F$, so $\{\overline{\mathfrak q}\}=V(\overline{\mathfrak q})$ is also closed. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-clopen-idempotent] there is an idempotent $e\in F$ with $D(e)=\{\overline{\mathfrak q}\}$; in particular $e\notin\overline{\mathfrak q}$, and $e\in\mathfrak Q$ for every prime $\mathfrak Q\ne\overline{\mathfrak q}$ of $F$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00PN (line 30293), first sentence ('Write $S\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)=S_1\times S_2$ ... as in Lemma 00PJ'), and proof of Lemma Tag 00PJ (lemma-isolated-point, line 30106), (1) => (2): Spec of a finite type algebra over a field is Jacobson, so the isolated point is closed, hence open and closed, and Lemma Tag 00EE (lemma-disjoint-decomposition, line 3858) gives the idempotent

proof.text: *The factor $eF$ is finite over $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$.* For every prime $\mathfrak Q$ of $F$ exactly one of $e$, $1-e$ lies in $\mathfrak Q$ (their product $0$ lies in $\mathfrak Q$, their sum $1$ does not), so $V(1-e)=D(e)=\{\overline{\mathfrak q}\}$. Let $B=F/(1-e)F$. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-quotient-homeomorphism-zero-locus] the primes of $B$ correspond to the points of $V(1-e)$, so $B$ has exactly one prime ideal; $B\ne0$, so a maximal ideal of $B$ exists, is prime, and equals that prime: every prime of $B$ is maximal. $B$ is a $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$-algebra of finite type (images of generators of $F$) [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], so by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-dim-zero-finite] $B$ is finite-dimensional over $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$; choose $b_1,\dots,b_n\in F$ whose images span $B$. For $f\in F$ write $f-\sum_i\lambda_ib_i=(1-e)y$ with $\lambda_i\in\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, $y\in F$; multiplying by $e$ and using $e(1-e)=0$ gives $ef=\sum_i\lambda_i\,eb_i$. So $eF$ is spanned over $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ by $eb_1,\dots,eb_n$ (in the source: $S_1=eF$ is finite over $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$).

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00PJ (lemma-isolated-point, line 30106), (1) => (2): '$S_1=S_{\mathfrak q}$ is a zero dimensional ring of finite type over $k$. Hence it is finite over $k$'; here by Lemma Tag 0ALW (lemma-finite-type-algebra-finite-nr-primes, line 14791) (1) => (5)

proof.text: *The factor $e'F'$ is finite over $\kappa(\mathfrak p')$.* Put $e'=\alpha(e)$, an idempotent of $F'$; by steps 4 and 5 ($e\notin\overline{\mathfrak q}$) $e'\notin\overline{\mathfrak q}'$. Let $B'=F'/(1-e')F'$. For $x\in F'$ write $x=\sum_k\mu_k\alpha(f_k)$ (step 3) and $ef_k=\sum_i\lambda_{ki}eb_i$ (step 6). Then $x\equiv e'x=\sum_k\mu_k\alpha(ef_k)=\sum_k\sum_i\mu_k\iota(\lambda_{ki})\alpha(eb_i)\pmod{(1-e')F'}$, using that $\alpha$ is a ring map with $\alpha(\lambda y)=\iota(\lambda)\alpha(y)$ (step 2). Hence the images of $\alpha(eb_1),\dots,\alpha(eb_n)$ span $B'$ over $\kappa(\mathfrak p')$: $B'$ is a finite $\kappa(\mathfrak p')$-algebra (the source's $S'_1$, a quotient of $S_1\otimes_{\kappa(\mathfrak p)}\kappa(\mathfrak p')$).

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00PN (lemma-four-rings, line 30293): 'This product decomposition induces a corresponding product decomposition for any $S\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$-algebra ... hence $S_i\otimes_{\kappa(\mathfrak p)}\kappa(\mathfrak p')\to S'_i$ is surjective. It follows that $S'_1$ is finite over $\kappa(\mathfrak p')$'

proof.text: *$\overline{\mathfrak q}'$ is isolated.* As in step 6, $V(1-e')=D(e')$ in $\operatorname{Spec}F'$, and $D(e')$ is open in the Zariski topology [def-weil-affine-spectrum]; $\overline{\mathfrak q}'\in D(e')$ by step 7. The field $\kappa(\mathfrak p')$ is a local ring whose only prime ideal is its maximal ideal $0$, and $B'$ is a finite $\kappa(\mathfrak p')$-algebra (step 7), so by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-over-zero-dim-local-discrete-spectrum] $\operatorname{Spec}B'$ is a finite discrete space. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-quotient-homeomorphism-zero-locus] $\operatorname{Spec}B'$ is homeomorphic to $V(1-e')=D(e')$ with the subspace topology; hence $D(e')$ is discrete, $\{\overline{\mathfrak q}'\}$ is open in $D(e')$, and, $D(e')$ being open in $\operatorname{Spec}F'$, $\{\overline{\mathfrak q}'\}$ is open in $\operatorname{Spec}F'=\operatorname{Spec}(S'\otimes_{R'}\kappa(\mathfrak p'))$. Since $R'\to S'$ is of finite type (step 1), this says that $R'\to S'$ is quasi-finite at $\mathfrak q'$ [def-weil-pbc-ring-map-quasi-finite-at-prime].

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00PN (lemma-four-rings, line 30293): '$\mathfrak q'$ corresponds to a point of $\Spec(S'_1)$ in the disjoint union decomposition $\Spec(S'\otimes_{R'}\kappa(\mathfrak p'))=\Spec(S'_1)\amalg\Spec(S'_2)$ (Lemma Tag 00ED, lemma-spec-product, line 3822). Since $S'_1$ is finite over a field ... $\Spec(S'_1)$ is a finite discrete set (Proposition Tag 00KJ). We conclude $\mathfrak q'$ is isolated in its fibre'

split_report.summary: Split following Algebra 00PN's proof (read at algebra.tex:30293) with 00PJ (1)=>(2) for the decomposition of the fibre ring. Eight steps: finite type of R'->S' and the compatibility of primes (elementary); the map alpha: F=S(x)_R k(p) -> F'=S'(x)_{R'} k(p') from the tensor universal property; F' spanned over k(p') by alpha(F) (the source's surjectivity, elementary); alpha^{-1} of the point of q' is the point of q (fibre-ring bijection); idempotent e with D(e)={q-bar} (isolated prime is maximal + clopen-idempotent); eF finite over k(p) via the quotient F/(1-e) with one prime and the new Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-dim-zero-finite (0ALW (1)=>(5)); e'=alpha(e) not in the point of q' and F'/(1-e') finite over k(p') (elementary); its Spec finite discrete and homeomorphic to the open D(e'), so q' is isolated. The source's products S_1 x S_2 are written with idempotents and quotients by 1-e. Statement unchanged; it already states that R'->S' is of finite type, which the source leaves implicit.
